1.sofaString: 102	Pt, *******, is a 4 year old male who is diagnosed with progressive heart failure with failing fontan physiology who is being referred for heart transplant Psychosocial Assessment.  Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the pt's adoptive father and review of the medical records.   SW spent 60 minutes of face to face time with patient and family.     Living situation:  **, *******, lives with his adoptive parents and siblings in *********, *******.  They reside in a single family home with 6 bedrooms and 4 bathrooms.  They have city water and central heating and a/c.  There is no smoking in the home.  They have 1 dog, a *******.         Demographics:  Mother: ****** *****  DOB:  **/**/****           Age:  52  Employment:  Retired  Phone:  ***-***-**** (cell)     Father: ****** *****  DOB:  **/**/****    Age:  69  Employment:  Retired  Phone:  ***-***-**** (cell)     Siblings:  Brother: ****** ***** **, age 14 (biological child of parents)  Sister:  ******* *****, age 14 (also adopted)     Support systems:     Parents report that they receive most of their support from one another and from their church family.  ****** is a ****** in their church.  The family also has a lot of extended family who reside locally.  They have 8 aunts and ****** residing in the ********* area.  In addition, ****** has an adult daughter, age 25, in *********.  She also has a 30 yr old daughter who resides in *** ****.  ****** has adult children residing in ************, *********, and *******.       ****** reports that he will be the one staying at bedside most of the time, while ****** stays home with the teens and assists them in getting to school etc.  He is on the waiting list for RMH but also plans to stay in the room with ******* much of the time.  Both parents have a car.  ****** denies that transportation to and from Gainesville will be a problem.  The only exception would be if ******* gets a donor offer while at home in *********.  He is concerned they would not be able to meet the time requirement to get him here in time.  He is amenable to ***** ****** as a potential alternate resource in this situation.         ****** disclosed that they were on a list to adopt and were provided background information on multiple children who needed a home.  He states they chose *******, knowing the medical history and likely road they would walk with him.  He states they had thought they would have more time before he would require transplant.  However, he states they knew what they were getting into when they adopted him and that they have no regrets.       In addition to his medical problems, ******* has also been diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder.  He is attending * ***-k program at **** ********** ****** and is doing ok.  He is able to communicate and talk.  He is not on any psychotropic meds at this time.  ****** states that his symptoms are mild in regards to the autism spectrum disorder.  SW observed ******* to **** out things he wanted.  He also was drawing on himself and the bed.  However, he seems to respond to ****** when he is redirected.  ****** appears to have realistic expectations for ******* and to be calm in addressing his behaviors.  ******* has not been in counseling or treatment for the autism disorder specifically, but was in ***** ***** and in **, **, and PT.  ******* has not yet been toilet trained, but is making progress on developmental milestones.      ******* enjoys playing with ******** and fire ******. He enjoys watching ****** the **** Engine shows.  He also likes to do things with his hands, building with blocks and using toy *******.  He enjoys music and art as well.       Course of illness:     ******* has a history signficant for heterotaxy with asplenia and situs inversus, history of malrotation s/p **** procedure and placement of GT, as well as history of factor VII deficiency, chronic diarrhea and prior cdiff infection, and complex congenital heart disease. Patient's congenital heart disease consists of unbalanced AV canal, ventricular inversion with double outlet morphologic left-sided RV dominance. He has undergone staged single ventricle palliative surgeries, including: PA banding, followed by bilateral *********** cavopulmonary anastomoses, followed by fenestrated extracardiac 18 mm ****** as well as *** repair. ****** procedure was complicated by thrombus within ****** circuit, for which patient remains chronically anticoagulated, and with persistent *** regurgitation. Patient was clinically doing well until */*/** when he developed low grade fever, *** symptoms of cough and congestion, as well as increased WOB. He went ** *** ** and was found to have lactic acidosis, hypoxemia with SpO2 in 60s, and profound hypoglycemia. Patient was managed with D10W bolus, volume resuscitation, supplemental O2 with NC, and IV Abx. Echo revealed moderate to severe *** regurgitation and severe ventricular ********** with EF 30%. Patient was found to be + rhinovirus and enterovirus. Patient was clinically volume overloaded with anasarca, pulmonary edema and effusions on CXR, and ascites on abdominal US. He was initiated on IV diuretic regimen with Lasix and started on Milrinone infusion. Due to concern for risk of decompensation, patient was transferred to ****** ****** for possible ECMO cannulation if needed. Patient did however remain hemodynamically stable. Milrinone gtt was increased at *** to 1mcg/kg/min and diuretic regimen was also increased. Ultimately end organ injury improved with resolution of pleural effusions and ascites as well as ********** in *** and ************. Patient did have ********** abnormalities, including hyponatremia that was managed with NaCl enteral supplementation. Patient was transferred to our facility at ** on */**/** for heart transplant evaluation and ongoing management of CHF.                 Financial Situation:     ******* is covered by Medicaid CMS insurance.  He does not receive SSI because he falls under his dad's social security benefits.  The family is supported financially by the retirement and social security benefits of the parents.  In addition, ****** continues to do some freelance work.       Family History:     ******* was adopted by these parents.  The adoption was finalized on ********* ****.  He was in ********** prior to the adoption.  There is no information about the medical history of the biological family.       This is a second marriage for these parents.  They both have adult children from previous marriages, as well as the two teens that they are raising together.        There is no reported mental health history, other than *******'s autism spectrum disorder.         There is no reported family history of drug or alcohol abuse.  There is no reported family history of DV or involvement with law enforcement. There is no reported history with DCF for child abuse or neglect.  For all of these, ****** reports that they would not have been allowed to adopt ****** children if they had any history in these areas.         Adherence:     There are no real concerns for adherence that were identified.  The family appears to be able to keep appointments and to meet the care needs for *******.  They have been consistent in administering medications and caring for his g-tube.  The primary concern is that ******* currently receives his meds through the g-tube.  He also receives the majority of his nutrition through the g-tube.  He takes very little by mouth.         Assessment and recommendations:     ****** states that he and ****** were aware of the possibility of transplant when they adopted *******.  He states they had thought it would have been farther down the road, however.  He states they have some apprehension about it, but understand the need.  They want to do what is best for *******.    ****** states that he is trying to learn what he can in order to help *******, but admits that he is a 'businessman' rather than a medical person.  He states that his wife does most of the care for ******* when they are at home.  He states that she will be here at the time of transplant, and that they will switch places so that she can be with him post-transplant while he cares for the teens at home.          IMPRESSION:     (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  1     Family Background & Social Support -  1     Financial/Insurance  - 1     Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 1     Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  1     Adherence - 2     Understanding of medical situation & transplant process -  2     Health Literacy -  1     Coping Skills - 1     Total:  11  Low     The family scores as low risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.       The primary concern is the challenge of getting ******* to take meds (such as prograf) by mouth.   Recommendations are listed below:     Recommendations:  *Provide ongoing education in simple terms to the family about heart transplant and post-transplant care.  Use teach-back method to ensure that the family understands what is being explained.  *Assist with connecting child and family with counseling and supports that will assist in positive coping skills in anticipation of a lengthy admission  *Assist ******* in taking oral medications by engaging Child **** and positive reinforcement/ reward system.  Assist caregivers in participating in this process.     ****** ******** LCSW  Pediatric Heart/ Lung Transplant Team  ***-***-****
